Analyse the dataset for the following insight:

INSIGHT TYPE: spatial_correlation
Does this indicator show significant GLOBAL spatial autocorrelation (clustering) across London boroughs? You are given the indicator's value per borough (DATASET_PATH) AND a borough adjacency list (ADJACENCY_PATH, columns: borough, neighbor -- each row means these two boroughs are geographic neighbors; the list is symmetric). Replace any missing values with the column mean first. Compute Global Moran's I: I = (n/S0) * [sum_i sum_j w_ij*(x_i-xbar)*(x_j-xbar)] / [sum_i (x_i-xbar)^2], using row-standardized weights w_ij = 1/(number of neighbors of borough i), and S0 = sum of all w_ij across every (i,j) pair in the adjacency list. Then estimate significance via permutation: shuffle the indicator values across boroughs (keep the adjacency list the same) at least 200 times, recompute I for each shuffle, and estimate a p-value as the fraction of shuffled I values that are >= your observed I (this mirrors a Monte Carlo Moran's I test). State FOUND (significant positive clustering, e.g. permutation p < 0.05 AND I > 0) or NOT FOUND, and cite your computed I and permutation p-value as evidence.


Dataset path (read-only): chunks_csv/moran_global_2023_crime.csv
IMPORTANT: each ```python``` block you write runs in its own fresh process with no memory of variables from earlier blocks. Always start each block by reloading what you need, e.g. df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH). pandas and numpy are pre-imported as pd and np. If you want to save a chart or file, save it into ARTIFACTS_DIR (already defined), never elsewhere.

Additional input file(s) available as variables: ADJACENCY_PATH (also read-only CSV paths, same rules as DATASET_PATH).

When you have enough evidence, respond with 'FINAL ANSWER:' followed by the JSON verdict described below.

When you give your FINAL ANSWER, it must be a single JSON object (nothing
else after it) matching this exact shape:

{
  "insight_present": true or false,
  "verdict_detail": "one or two sentence plain-English summary of your finding",
  "evidence": [
    {"description": "what you computed", "value": <the actual number>},
    ... (at least one entry -- you MUST cite a real number you computed with code)
  ]
}

Do not include any text after the closing brace. Example:

FINAL ANSWER:
{"insight_present": true, "verdict_detail": "Site X is a statistical outlier.",
 "evidence": [{"description": "modified z-score for Site X", "value": 4.12},
              {"description": "threshold used", "value": 3.0}]}
